review_notes: Read the whole target file and grepped the CoulombIonization tree for the same Sigma/comap pattern. It appears in at least five other files: ActualBandInverseBarrier, ExpandedAnnulusCapExcess, ExpandedAnnulusCapNumerics (variant), AnnularEventNumericsBarrier and others. I read three of them in full. I did not read the other occurrences, so their exact shapes are unverified. The `actual_expandedAnnulus_inverse_eventually` proof and the net-union proof are one-off and not duplicated. Nothing here was compiled. The proposed lemma's exact universe and unification behaviour is untested, and the rewritten uses are sketches. The lemma only absorbs the final step (the `eventually_comap` extraction and packing into the subtype). The `A`, `π`, `L`, `hb` and transport lines still need a per-theorem choice unless a bigger abstraction is introduced.

findings.problem: The proof turns a pointwise-in-index eventual statement (`actual_expandedAnnulus_inverse_eventually`, where `j` and `y` are functions of the index) into a statement uniform in `j` and `y`. It does this by building a Sigma type of admissible parameters, comapping `l` along `Sigma.fst`, applying the pointwise theorem on that filter, and extracting with `Filter.eventually_comap` followed by `hi ⟨i,⟨(j,y),…⟩⟩ rfl`. The same argument appears nearly verbatim in ActualBandInverseBarrier.actual_band_inverse_uniform_eventually, ExpandedAnnulusCapExcess.actual_expandedAnnulus_cap_excess_uniform_eventually and ExpandedAnnulusCapNumerics.own_probability_expandedAnnulus_cap_uniform_eventually. Each copy re-declares `A`, `π`, `L`, `ht`, `hb`, `he` and the closing `filter_upwards … exact hi ⟨i,…⟩ rfl`. The final step is the part that is the same everywhere: from `∀ᶠ q in comap Sigma.fst l, P q.1 q.2.1` to `∀ᶠ i in l, ∀ a, C i a → P i a`. It is re-proved by hand in every file.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general lemma, e.g. in a small shared file imported by these modules:

theorem eventually_forall_of_eventually_comap_sigma {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {α : ι → Type*} {C P : ∀ i, α i → Prop}
    (h : ∀ᶠ q : (Σ i, {a : α i // C i a}) in Filter.comap Sigma.fst l, P q.1 q.2.1) :
    ∀ᶠ i in l, ∀ a, C i a → P i a := by
  filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_comap.mp h] with i hi a ha
  exact hi ⟨i, ⟨a, ha⟩⟩ rfl

Then the target's tail (lines 100–103) becomes:
  have := eventually_forall_of_eventually_comap_sigma (C := fun i (p : Fin (K i) × Space) => (2:ℝ)^p.1.val*r₀ i ≤ s i ∧ ((2:ℝ)^p.1.val*r₀ i)/2 ≤ ‖p.2‖ ∧ ‖p.2‖ ≤ B*((2:ℝ)^p.1.val*r₀ i)) (P := fun i p => OriginalPointInverseBounds (F i) (Z i) (lam i) (r₀ i) (s i) c₁ h xi p.1 p.2) hh
  filter_upwards [this] with i hi j y hjs hyl hyu
  exact hi (j,y) ⟨hjs,hyl,hyu⟩

The sibling proofs use the same one-line extraction. For ExpandedAnnulusCapNumerics the index is `ℝ × Space × ℝ`, so `α i` is not `Fin (K i) × Space` there. The `hb` and transport lines (`hs0.comp ht`, `ht.eventually hstate`) stay per theorem. To also share those, define one named predicate `AnnulusAdmissible r₀ s B i (p : Fin (K i) × Space)` for the three `Fin`×`Space` uses, so `A` and `hb` are not re-spelled.
findings.benefit: The subtle step (comap along `Sigma.fst`, `rfl` witness, repacking the subtype) is proved once and named, instead of being copied into at least four theorems. A reader sees at once that each theorem is the routine pointwise-to-uniform upgrade. If the admissibility condition or the filter construction changes, there is one place to fix. The cost is one new lemma and a slightly longer call site.
